rationale: This is the book-equity analogue of the already-tested "Conservative Depreciation Earnings Yield," and because one year of abnormal depreciation is minuscule relative to ceq, the signal will be nearly indistinguishable from plain book-to-market — a cosmetic variant that mostly rediscovers value.

This is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived "Underdepreciation Earnings Reliance Trap" (MA replaced by TS_MAX), and because TS_MAX minus current is always non-negative, the interaction loses the abnormality interpretation and instead loads on the level/volatility of depreciation intensity.

The sign logic is internally inconsistent: a positive txach means tax expense charged against ib exceeds cash taxes paid, which makes reported *earnings* conservative (it boosts oancf, not ib), so pairing it with an earnings-yield rank and a negative expected sign contradicts the stated mechanism.

This is a direct base-yield swap of the already-tested "Opaque Other Accrual Earnings Trap" (ib → ceq), which the archive shows to be a weak channel, and it adds no new economic content beyond the substitution.

It is essentially the sign-flipped mirror of the archived "Receivable Reliance Revenue Trap," and its economics directly contradict the sibling "Inventory Liquidation Cash Yield Trap" logic (working-capital release treated as good here, unsustainable there) without resolving which interpretation holds.

The expression matches the hypothesis and sign (apalch positive = payables-funded cash inflow, interacted with cheap-on-cash-flow rank, expected negative), and it is a substantively motivated short-side reformulation of the previously failed long-side payables adjustments, though it remains close to prior work on the same channel.
